narrative.title: The Overpass Headcount Scan
narrative.scenario: A drone photographs a tree-shaped car-wash lane network from directly overhead. Each lane sits one column left or right of its parent, and taller upstream lanes hide the lanes beneath them in the same column. The traffic office wants the visible lane numbers, reading the photo from leftmost column to rightmost — the first lane encountered from the sky in each column wins.
narrative.inputFormat: The root of a binary tree given as a level-order array where null marks a missing child. The root sits at column 0.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array of visible values, one per column, ordered left to right.

testCases.explanation: Columns -2..2 show 4, 2, the root 1 (which shades 5 and 6), 3, and 7.
The root sits above 4 in column 0, so 1 stays visible while 4 hides.

hintLevels: Level 1: Visibility means being the topmost node in your column — depth hides everything below it.
Level 2: Walk level by level with a column counter (left child -1, right child +1) and claim each column only the first time.
Level 3: A map keyed by column filled during BFS gives topmost holders; emit keys in sorted order for the final readout.
